round_label: chapter fill hypothesis 2, /map off the flag, /paintings' corridor bleed
notes: Wil's device pass of 2026-09-18, all three items. ITEM 2 (/map) APPROVED ON THE DEVICE -- 'the map page is perfect' -- so T comes off the ?glass=1 flag and ships as the default on /map; the landing script's flag gate is removed with it. No other change to that page. ITEM 1 (chapters) FAILED: the strip parked fully off-screen at top:-12px was invisible but Safari did not sample it, so the client brief's section 8.2 claim (an element past the edge is still read) does not hold on iOS 26.6.1 -- the third published claim about this build to fail here. HYPOTHESIS 2, the one combination never tried: ON screen at the edge so it qualifies, and z-index:-1 so <main>'s opaque ground (round 14) covers it at every scroll depth. That is the configuration that produced the original unkillable bands on /map and /paintings, minus the visibility. STILL UNKNOWN: if what Wil sees is the bar MINIMIZING rather than the sampler declining, no element can fix it -- A2 measured that a minimized bar covers nothing. Worth one check because it is free and invisible either way. ITEM 3 (/paintings) BUILT, behind ?glass=1. Mirrors the map faithfully, and the faithful part is which box grows: the map's UI layer keeps its original box and only the canvas extends, with the camera taking the extra back. Here the STAGE must keep its box because stage.clientHeight is the composition basis -- it picks the FOV, the portrait and phone thresholds, the walk's scroll total and the sheet-UI split -- so only the canvas grows. camera.setViewOffset(w, h, 0, 0, w, h + B) is three.js's exact equivalent of the map camera's padding: with aspect left at w/h it multiplies the frustum height by (h+B)/h from the same top edge, so the canvas's top h rows are framed pixel-for-pixel as today and the extra B rows show world BELOW. The stage takes overflow:visible under the flag so it stops clipping the taller canvas. THE OPEN QUESTION: the stage is sticky, and A2 measured a pinned box's overflow clipped at the visual viewport (160px requested, 21px rendered). This may be clipped the same way. What differs is that the canvas is a real absolutely-positioned child with its own box rather than bleed out of the stage's -- the configuration the map proves in flow, untested while pinned. If it is clipped, only un-sticking the corridor can work and the framing is untouched either way. allowedRoutes stays empty: B and T are both 0 in Chromium, so every route must stay pixel-identical.
